issues.quote: I understand it had stopped when they found him. A regulator stops with its master, Inspector.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says nothing about the upstairs regulator or its state when the body was found.
issues.misreading: A solver could take the stopped regulator as a clock reading marking the time of the death or the time of the attack, and try to fit that reading against the watch and hall-clock facts. The sheet gives no such reading.

issues.quote: Whoever did this was not in a hurry
issues.fact: The sheet gives no information about how long the killer took or how much time they had.
issues.misreading: The phrase suggests the killer had a long, unhurried stretch of time, which a solver could use as a duration hint between the 10:45 departure and the 11:00 strike.

issues.quote: It strikes by its own face. Aurèle was fond of it for that.
issues.fact: The sheet only says the hall clock struck eleven a moment after Dr Vauthier sat down. It does not say how the hall clock relates to his watch or to the temple bell.
issues.misreading: The remark could be read as saying the hall clock runs on its own time, separate from the watch, so a solver might doubt that its strike is comparable to the watch readings.
